questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The crucial aspects in choosing my study destination were the academic profile of the University of San Diego School of Law, the opportunity to strengthen my international and comparative legal skills, and the overall study environment in San Diego.

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used the platform Zillow. AirBnB cannot be recommended

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Sign a lease instead of renting on AirBnB

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process is very easy. You have a call beforehand with the person in charge of the exchange program. On this call the person assign you to your desired courses. You then show up, buy/rent the books and you are good to go.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help in regard to basically everything except for housing.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses that I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose wisely. Research the courses thoroughly beforehand in regard to the exam type, day of classes etc. Some courses are definitely more difficult than others. So choose according to your ambition.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: At some courses the level is high, on others the level is low. It really depends on the subject and professor.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style is very different. In the U.S. the professor use the Socratic Method (cold calling), so be prepared for class assignments. The professor's structure their courses completely by themselves - they are very enthusiastic.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Intro to U.S. Law 
Legal Writing & Research
Finance & Accounting for Lawyers 
Securities Regulation
International Business Transactions

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Intro to U.S. Law is mandatory. 

Legal Writing & Research is very assignment based (there is no exam). It is a pass/fail class. 

Finance & Accounting for Lawyers is based upon calculations in connection to accounting and finance (preferably for students who likes to use a calculator). 

Securities Regulation is a difficult course. Lots of reading (approximately over 1.500 pages) and tough exam. The professor is though really good and inspiring. 

International Business Transactions is a good class for UCPH students as the course revolves around concepts that are somewhat similar to the ones covered at UCPH. So a MA student from UCPH definitely has an advantage when taking this course. This is though based on what classes the student participated in at UCPH.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: VAT on all sorts of products. Prices do not include VAT, so be aware of that. It is not like in Denmark where the price includes VAT.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Renting a flat is definitely more expensive than in Denmark. If you want to live comfortably expect to spend +- 10.000 DKK. This will though give you a place in a safe area where you can have your own room.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great sport facilities!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can imagine. All sport activities is available. There is not a lot of social activities of the kind we know them in Denmark.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Use the gym - the facilities is great! Also a great soccer field.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit Grand Canyon, Sion National Park, go to Mexico for 1 day, travel around San Diego (PB, MB, La Jolla, Del Mar and North Park).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. I experienced San Diegans as very polite and open minded. They are very extroverted and open for conversation.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and proactive. Do not hesitate to propose social activities. People will not reject you in a bad manner.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The fact that the culture is very social.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be openminded. 
Reach out - be proactive. 
Ask former exchange students that went to USD where to go so you don't waste time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The professors are very helpful and like to engage with the students. Use this opportunity to discuss ideas, get perspectives etc.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing a society that is filled with decency and politeness.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Can't think of one.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
